# Orbit Store (Beta)

> A modern PS5 download manager with resumable downloads and phone controls. Orbit runs on the console as an ELF service, with a native PS5 TV app and a browser interface on the local network.

The official project is maintained at https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5. The public repository contains documentation and the Orbit payload feed. Releases attach orbit_store.elf, the native PPSA99177.ffpkg, SHA-256 checksums and a complete source/licence bundle for both programs and their open-source components.

Orbit requires a PS5 environment capable of loading homebrew ELF payloads. Full console transfers, reboot/auto-start acceptance and other firmware versions remain unverified in this beta. See the current release notes for validation details.

Run orbit_store.elf through a payload manager or ELF loader, then open Orbit Store from the PS5 Media tab. Phone and computer controls are available at http://<ps5-ip>:34177/ on the same local network. Pair devices keeps the code visible on the PS5; Show code on PS5 repeats its notification.

Version 0.8.0 adds optional TorBox downloads, ten interface languages, Discover as the opening page with Latest releases and a paged All games grid, refined native/browser controls and rest-mode listener recovery. Keep the PS5 awake during transfers; this does not add downloads during rest mode. The native app version is 1.2.0 and includes service 0.8.0. Copy PPSA99177.ffpkg to /data/homebrew/ and open it from the Games row using kstuff and ShadowMountPlus. A compatible ELF loader on port 9021 lets it start the bundled service; an older running service needs an intentional restart. Orbit offers 602 games with single-file FFPFSC and exFAT options from Archive.org and Vikingfile, plus Fileditch Folder dumps that Orbit extracts and installs automatically after the download. Browse sorts by verified release date, newest first, with undated titles afterward.

The interface supports English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Turkish. Native Orbit follows the PS5 system language at launch. Browser App settings → Language sets a per-device preference or follows the browser automatically. Game metadata and provider pages may keep their original language.

Connect TorBox in browser App settings → Debrid. Both apps then offer TorBox for supported download options. Account plans, host availability and quotas apply. Direct provider downloads remain available. Keep using 0.8.0 or later while TorBox jobs remain in queue/history; older apps cannot read them.

Library shows installed games and drive sources, with scan, mount/unmount and copy/move actions when supported by a compatible ShadowMount v1 local API. Storage shows capacity and game sizes measured on request. Library and storage operations have local fixture coverage; console acceptance remains pending.

Payload-manager integration is opt-in. App settings → Payload managers → Add Orbit adds and keeps a copy current in Payload Manager or Homebrew Launcher. Existing copies do not imply consent. Stop syncing preserves files and auto-start settings. Auto-start is separate, and Orbit never changes Payload Manager's global switch. The reported etaHEN toggle interaction remains under investigation.

Catalogue additions and updated links arrive automatically. App settings → Game catalogue → Refresh catalogue checks for additions manually. The last available catalogue remains accessible offline; an internet connection is needed to download games. Queued downloads keep the files originally chosen. App features and fixes still require an Orbit update. To restore a deleted Orbit icon, start Orbit through the payload manager; settings and the download queue stay saved.

Orbit supports four connections for new large downloads when the host supports ranges and a strong file identity. Existing partials keep their original layout; other downloads use one connection. Direct-only queues require 0.7.0 or later; queues or history containing TorBox jobs require 0.8.0 or later. It also fixes Browse search navigation: Up returns to the page tab, Down enters results or collection controls, and Left/Right keep text editing.

The browser version checks for updates on opening and displays a dismissible notice when a newer version is available. Installation and restart remain manual. After upgrading, use 0.4.2 or later because older builds cannot read its saved queue format.

App settings includes Update / reinstall. A paired user can check the fixed official release feed, download a checksum-verified ELF, and see running versus saved versions. Stop Orbit to restart preserves the paused queue; the user then starts /data/orbit-store/orbit_store.elf or an opted-in synced copy from their payload manager. Manually imported copies outside sync need replacing by the user. Older installations need one manual ELF replacement and Orbit restart to get these controls.

Downloads go directly from third-party providers to the console's selected storage. Orbit supports a persistent reorderable queue, Active/Finished/Failed/Cancelled views, pause, resume, retry countdowns and history cleanup without deleting completed files. Storage estimates include unfinished downloads. Browse has source/format/size filters, release-date/title/size sorting and shared favourites. It does not directly install game packages, launch games, or download in rest mode. Fileditch Folder downloads are extracted automatically after the download. A confirmed ShadowMount scan may register or mount discovered games. Use it only for material you are entitled to obtain and use. Orbit is independent of Sony, PlayStation, game publishers and download providers.

Orbit Store is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later. The complete source corresponding to each released ELF and native FFPKG, copyleft dependency sources, licence notices and rebuild instructions are included with that release.

Vikingfile file-page options require Orbit 0.5.0 or later. Choose a drive and Open download page on PS5, complete verification if requested, press Download on Vikingfile, then return to Orbit and open Downloads. Orbit validates the exact file before queueing it. The provider browser runs on PS5 even when started from a paired device. Sources remain opt-in. Fileditch Folder options arrive through catalogue updates, need a Fileditch-enabled build and follow the same open-on-PS5 flow; Orbit extracts and installs them after the download.

Diagnostics in App settings lets the user view and copy a local report. Reports omit pairing codes, access tokens, download links, game names and paths; they are not sent automatically.

Orbit 0.8.0 uses the current catalogue feed. Earlier apps retain their bundled or saved catalogue but require an app update for future catalogue revisions. Metadata corrections arrive without reinstalling 0.8.0.

The native app shares the catalogue, queue, favourites and Library with the browser version. Native App settings includes Download sources, Storage, Pair a device, Game catalogue and Updates. More settings opens browser-only setup and diagnostics. Vikingfile and Fileditch browser options carry the selected game, source and destination into the browser; opening it never starts a download. Browser App settings → TV app installs or updates the native FFPKG; close the TV app before replacement. Native App settings → Updates has separate TV app and download service controls. Restarts require confirmation. The 0.6 browser interface displays a dismissible native-app announcement linking to the GitHub release.

## Documentation

- [Project overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/README.md): Features, current screenshots, setup, controls and beta limits.
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/guides/getting-started.md): Installation, Payload Manager, updates and phone pairing.
- [Downloads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/guides/downloads.md): Browse, sources, formats, Vikingfile and Fileditch PS5 browser steps, storage and queue controls.
- [Library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/guides/library.md): Inventory labels and compatible ShadowMount actions.
- [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/guides/troubleshooting.md): Startup, updates, providers, storage, artwork and diagnostics.
- [Official project](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5): Public repository and project updates.

## Downloads

- [Current release](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest): Version, changelog, validation notes, source archives and licence bundle.
- [Current ELF](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/orbit_store.elf): The Orbit application payload.
- [Native TV app](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/PPSA99177.ffpkg): The Games-row app, including the Orbit service.
- [TV app SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/PPSA99177.ffpkg.sha256): Verify the FFPKG before installing.
- [ELF SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/releases/latest/download/orbit_store.elf.sha256): Verify the downloaded payload before loading it.
- [Payload Manager feed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/main/payloads.json): Add this URL in Payload Manager under Settings, Manage Sources, Add Source. The feed contains Orbit's ELF URL, version and checksum.

## Support

- [Issues](https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/issues): Report problems with the Orbit version, PS5 firmware, loader and steps to reproduce. Keep pairing codes and private information out of reports.

## Optional

- [Payload Manager custom repository guide](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-payload-manager/blob/main/CUSTOM_REPOSITORIES.md): Upstream feed format and source setup instructions.
